title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover + defrag coordinator (heuristics v25)
author: Marina Patel
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and reactive eviction under load have been causing tail latency spikes and increased GPU memory churn on long-running conversations. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes (heuristics v25) to reduce fragmentation, enable background compaction, introduce async spillover/paging to host memory, and make eviction decisions workload-aware so we avoid evicting high-hit prefixes. Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive eviction tiers: add a 3-tier eviction decision pipeline (hot, warm, cold) that considers hit-rate, recency, and prefix length weight. Prevents premature eviction of high-reuse prefixes. 2) Defrag coordinator: central background task that schedules lightweight compaction tasks across shards to coalesce small free regions without pausing inference. Uses a budgeted work-quantum to avoid interference with runtime threads. 3) Async host spillover (paging): introduce an optional spillover allocator that pages cold KV blocks to pinned host memory using an async migration thread pool; includes backpressure signals so scheduling/batching avoids thrashing. 4) Fragmentation-aware compaction: compaction now targets regions with high fragmentation_ratio and rebalances allocations to reduce future external fragmentation. 5) Heuristic tuning & telemetry: expose new knobs and metrics (kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.paging.latency, kv.cache.evictions_by_tier, kv.cache.compaction_cycles) and a feature flag kv_adaptive_spillover_v25 behind canary rollout. 6) Scheduling integration: the batch scheduler now consults the KV manager's memory headroom signal to make burst vs. queue decisions, reducing p99 increase when memory pressure spikes. Implementation notes: - runtime/kv_cache/*: refactor of KVCacheManager state machine, added tiered eviction policy, API to mark prefixes as pinned or warm. - runtime/kv_cache/defrag_coordinator.rs: new coordinator that runs compact tasks with a budgeted timer. - runtime/kv_cache/spillover.rs: spillover allocator and async pager using tokio threadpool, marshalled via bounded channel. - runtime/scheduler/batcher.rs: consults kv_manager.memory_headroom() and adjusts max_batch_size when spillover is active. - benchmarks/kv_memory_v25.yaml: new perf harness to measure end-to-end effect under sustained chat load. Benchmarks and results: - Canary runs on dedicated pool (g4dn-like) show: 12% reduction in end-to-end p99 latency for long-context workloads (>8k tokens), 18% reduction in median token latency under high-concurrency mixed workloads, and ~27% user-visible decline in active GPU memory fragmentation (measured by fragmentation_ratio). Paging adds an average 2.4ms host-read overhead for cold prefixes but reduces large eviction thrashing. Rollout plan: - Feature flag kv_adaptive_spillover_v25 default off. - Canary: 5% traffic on dedicated pools for 72h monitoring metrics. - Gradual rollout with automated rollback if kv.cache.paging.latency_p95 > 50ms or kv.cache.eviction_rate increases >2x. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for eviction policy decision logic - [x] Integration test for async spillover correctness under synthetic loads - [x] E2E perf harness added and green - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated (internally) - [x] Docs: added runtime/kv_cache/README.md describing knobs and operator guidance Related: ENG-2315 (reduce p99 under long contexts) and ENG-1987 (defrag coordinator prototype). Known limitations: - Spillover currently requires host memory backing and is not enabled for on-prem air-gapped installs without operator approval. - Under extremely tight host memory the pager will block and cause increases to latency; the rollout policy guards against this. Merge notes: squash-merged into main, changelog updated.

release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adds fragmentation-aware compaction, a defrag coordinator, async spillover/paging to host memory, and adaptive eviction tiers which reduces p99 latency for long-context workloads. Feature is behind kv_adaptive_spillover_v25 flag and will be canaried.
monitoring_runbooks: Monitor kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio and kv.cache.eviction_rate after rollout
If kv.cache.paging.latency_p95 > 50ms or eviction_rate > 2x baseline -> trigger rollback and investigate host memory pressure
notes: This PR consolidates several previous experiment branches (defrag prototype ENG-1987, paging experiment ENG-2173) into a production-ready implementation with conservative defaults. The approach favors gradual rollout and operator visibility.
size_impact: binary: +750KB (runtime), allocs: minor increase in host memory footprint when enabled
testing: Unit + integration + canary perf harness included; CI shows green. Load testing on dedicated pools run for 72h as part of canary.
